story: List of YouTube channels for improving web development and programming skills
text: I have recently discovered [tsoding twitch channel]( [LINK] ) which describes itself as Recreational programming. The topics range from webassembly and Game development to functional programming in haskell and ocaml. Some of the interesting random things I found there include: * [a parser combinator in haskell]( [VIDEO] ) * [stack based language compiler in ocaml]( [LINK] ) You can find all the things that were done during the streams in [LINK] . You can also find his schedule at [LINK]
Nice to see Tsoding on the front page. He has another great video that covers a bunch of topics while making a JSON parser with only the Haskell standard library: [VIDEO]

To understand monads, I think it helps to know a language where expressing such a concept is more natural. Although I do not claim to know 100% what monads are yet, coming across these features made it easier for me to understand the concept a little bit. - Algebraic data types - OCaml's let expressions - F#'s computation expressions I also think that it is important to write something that naturally requires the use of monads. One thing that spring to mind is Parser Combinators. - [LINK] - [VIDEO]
